title: Propagation, vanishing, generation and linear multiplication for regular coherent sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq0$, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and $\mathcal F$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] on $\mathbf P^n_k$. Write $\mathcal F(d)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal O(d)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and let $H^j$ denote module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. Assume
$$H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(a-j))=0\quad(1\leq j\leq n).$$
For every integer $b\geq a$, $\mathcal F$ is $b$-regular, i.e. $H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(b-j))=0$ for $1\leq j\leq n$. For all $d\geq a$ and $j>0$ one has $H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(d))=0$. For every $b\geq a$ the evaluation morphism
$$H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(b))\otimes_k\mathcal O\longrightarrow\mathcal F(b)$$
is surjective, as is the natural multiplication map
$$H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(b))\otimes_k H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal O(1))\longrightarrow H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal F(b+1)).$$

source.place: Tags 08A6 (lemma-m-regular-up), 08A7 (lemma-m-regular-multiply), 08A8 (lemma-m-regular-globally-generated), with Tag 08A3 (definition-regularity); cohomology in degrees greater than n vanishes by the ordered standard affine-cover Cech calculation, coherent.tex Tag 01XD (lemma-cech-cohomology-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: First prove, simultaneously for all fields and all integers $m$, the following two assertions by induction on $n$: an $m$-regular sheaf is $(m+1)$-regular, and its degree-$m$ linear multiplication is surjective. For $n=0$, regularity has no conditions. The single standard chart is $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and every twist has its global basis $e_0^{(d)}$; multiplication by the basis of $H^0(\mathcal O(1))=k$ is an isomorphism. Higher cohomology vanishes by the cohomology bound. A quasi-coherent sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the sheaf of its vector space of global sections, so its evaluation is surjective. This also settles all remaining conclusions when $n=0$.

We may use any field extension $K/k$ in these two induction assertions. The pullback $\mathcal F_K$ is quasi-coherent by the pullback node. Its local finite generating families pull back to finite generating families: tensor a local surjection from a finite free module, and the images of its basis still generate the tensor product. Standard chart rings $K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ are Noetherian by the finite-type algebra node, since a field has only two ideals. Thus the coherent-versus-quasi-coherent-finite-type node shows $\mathcal F_K$ is coherent. The same argument shows twists are coherent, since they are locally copies of $\mathcal F$.

source.place: 08A4 and 08A7, field extension; coherent pullback hypotheses

proof.text: Apply flat base change to $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for every $\mathcal F(d)$ and for $\mathcal O(1)$. The first morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by its finite standard affine cover with affine overlaps; the second is flat because tensoring vector spaces is exact. The gluing bases of the twists identify their pullbacks with the same twists over $K$. Pullback commutes with tensor products of modules, so $(\mathcal F(d))_K=(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal O(d))_K\cong\mathcal F_K\otimes\mathcal O_K(d)=\mathcal F_K(d)$, with $u\otimes e\mapsto u_K\otimes e_K$ on local sections. We obtain $H^j(\mathcal F_K(d))\cong H^j(\mathcal F(d))\otimes_k K$. For $j=0$ the comparison sends $u\otimes c$ to $c\,u_K$; multiplication consequently sends $(u\otimes c)\otimes(v\otimes e)$ to $(uv)\otimes ce$. Thus the multiplication map over $K$ is exactly the scalar extension of the map over $k$. Scalar extension by a field extension detects zero vector spaces and surjectivity: choose a basis of a nonzero vector space, or of the cokernel, and its scalar extension remains nonzero. These statements also show the regularity hypothesis is preserved. Take $K=k(t)$, which is infinite since its distinct powers of $t$ are distinct. It therefore suffices to prove the two induction assertions over infinite fields.

Now let $n>0$, assume the induction assertions in dimension $n-1$ over every field, and work over an infinite field. Apply the hyperplane-sequence node to $\mathcal F$ to obtain $s,H,i,\mathcal G$. For $1\leq j\leq n-1$, its sequence at $d=m-j$ contains
$$H^j(\mathcal F(m-j))\longrightarrow H^j(\mathcal G(m-j))\longrightarrow H^{j+1}(\mathcal F(m-j-1)).$$
The outer terms vanish by $m$-regularity, since $1\leq j<j+1\leq n$. Exactness gives the middle vanishing. Thus $\mathcal G$ is $m$-regular on $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$.

By the dimension induction hypothesis, $\mathcal G$ is $(m+1)$-regular. For $1\leq j\leq n$, the hyperplane sequence at $d=m+1-j$ gives
$$H^j(\mathcal F(m-j))\longrightarrow H^j(\mathcal F(m+1-j))\longrightarrow H^j(\mathcal G(m+1-j)).$$
The left term vanishes by the assumption on $\mathcal F$. For $j<n$, the right term vanishes by $(m+1)$-regularity of $\mathcal G$; for $j=n$ it vanishes by the cohomology bound on $\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$. Exactness therefore gives $(m+1)$-regularity of $\mathcal F$. Descend this result to the original field using step 3. Repeating the one-step assertion $b-a$ times proves $b$-regularity for every $b\geq a$.

For the multiplication assertion in dimension $n$, let $t\in H^0(P,\mathcal F(m+1))$. By step 4 and dimension induction for multiplication, write its restriction as $\overline t=\sum_

proof.text:
It remains to prove generation, now over the original field. Choose a finite quotient $ igoplus_{
u=1}^r\mathcal O(-m_
u)	woheadrightarrow\mathcal F$ from the quotient-by-twists node (a field is Noetherian). Fix $b\geq a$ and choose $d\geq b$ and $d\geq m_
u$ for every $
u$. Tensoring the quotient with $\mathcal O(d)$ preserves surjectivity: locally it is tensoring with a free rank-one module. The twist-tensor isomorphism identifies its source with $ igoplus_
u\mathcal O(d-m_
u)$. For every nonnegative integer $e$, the global coordinate monomials of degree $e$ generate $\mathcal O(e)$: on $D_+(x_i)$, $x_i^e$ is its basis. Thus the images of these finitely many monomials generate $\mathcal F(d)$. If $r=0$, the quotient already says $\mathcal F=0$.

By step 6 at each degree $b,b+1,\ldots,d-1$, every section of $\mathcal F(d)$ is a finite sum $\sum_\alpha f_\alpha v_{\alpha,1}\cdots v_{\alpha,d-b}$ with $f_\alpha\in H^0(P,\mathcal F(b))$ and $v_{\alpha,q}\in H^0(P,\mathcal O(1))$; this follows by expanding one preimage tensor at each degree. On $U_i=D_+(x_i)$ trivialize all twists by powers of $x_i$. The section above divided by $x_i^{d-b}$ becomes
$$\sum_\alpha f_\alpha|_{U_i}\prod_q(v_{\alpha,q}/x_i).$$
Every coefficient is a regular function on $U_i$. Since sections of $\mathcal F(d)$ generate and division by $x_i^{d-b}$ identifies $\mathcal F(d)|_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal F(b)|_{U_i}$, the restrictions of global sections of $\mathcal F(b)$ generate on $U_i$. The $U_i$ cover $P$, so the evaluation map is surjective. For $d=b$, the products are empty and equal to $1$. This proves generation for every $b\geq a$.
